# Tusker Docs

Generated catalog of published documentation routes.

- Dispatcher pseudocode | /developer/internals/dispatcher-pseudocode/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-22
  Reference algorithm for a cron-driven binary that turns the vault's dashboard.json into agent runs. This is the contract the Tusker CLI exposes; the dispatcher does not hand-parse markdown.
  source: skill/docs/DISPATCHER_PSEUDOCODE.md
  tags: internals

- Failure classes and recovery table | /developer/internals/failure-classes/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-22
  Every tusker release --to failed|stalled|cancelled takes a --failure-class that drives retry and escalation behavior. The enum is frozen in schema.go.
  source: skill/docs/FAILURE_CLASSES.md
  tags: internals

- Operator intervention | /developer/internals/operator-intervention/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  The dispatcher and tusker CLI cover the steady-state loop. When things wedge — a retry budget exhausts, a human needs to cancel a run mid-flight, or somebody hand-edits a note — a human operator steps in. This doc is the audit-trail contract for those interventions so the vault history stays truthful.
  source: skill/docs/OPERATOR_INTERVENTION.md
  tags: internals

- Orchestration runbook | /developer/internals/orchestration-runbook/ | audience: developer | updated: 2026-04-28
  This is the operator contract for ORC-era agent runs. The current vault note stays the durable work record; runtime state lives in the daemon store and run artifacts. Do not smuggle live process state into frontmatter because that turns markdown into a bad database.
  source: skill/docs/ORCHESTRATION_RUNBOOK.md
  tags: internals

  tags: internals, design

- Bases — editing and extending | /user/reference/bases/ | audience: user | updated: 2026-04-22

  source: skill/references/BASES.md
